correctness.rationale: All 495 possible eight-subsets were evaluated from the graph adjacency, yielding exactly 252 tetrahedral facets and full f-vector (12,66,204,252). Sixteen missing triangles have verifiable cone fillings, giving simply connected two-skeleton and second-boundary rank 55. An independently rebuilt exact signed boundary has 143 unimodular pivots and zero residual; its image is primitive and the code verifies boundary composition over Z and mod-two rank. Hence integral reduced homology is Z^6 in degree two and Z^109 in degree three. Hurewicz/Whitehead and primitive attaching-map basis reduction give the claimed mixed wedge. See CHECK.py and CHECK_OUTPUT.txt; no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The same-object indexed three-cut result and separate total-three-cut study concern different threshold and definition, respectively; neither provides an implication to ordinary eight-cut homotopy. The founding primary cut-complex paper (arXiv:2304.13675) covers named graph families but not this truncated-tetrahedral eight-cut, and its Theorem 6.1 hypothesis fails at the sixteen absent triangles. The sequel (arXiv:2407.08158) treats disjoint unions, squared paths and grids. Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches for exact object/aliases, general cubic-graph coverage and nearest cut theories, plus web searches for the object, did not reveal a stronger result. Failed search is not proof of uniqueness; the accessible indexed same-object summaries are not substituted for full-text noncoverage.

value.rationale: At the natural eight-cut (four-vertex-complement) threshold of the truncated tetrahedron, an exact pure three-dimensional graph-cut complex has genuine homotopy in two distinct degrees: six S2 and 109 S3. The lower-dimensional spheres obstruct Cohen–Macaulayness and shellability, and exhibit a finite structural boundary not settled by the published cut-complex complete-skeleton criterion. This is a complete motivated integral homotopy invariant for a canonical polyhedral graph, not an arbitrary sample or a known Betti table.
